purpose: Holdout journalist abduction probes used to compare live forensic output and abduction-map behavior against additional resolved real-world cases without altering the original six-case validation gate.

sources.title: Abducted in Iraq
sources.notes: CPJ's Iraq abduction report summarizes multiple resolved journalist kidnappings including Phil Sands, Meutya Hafid, Budiyanto, Richard Butler, and the Romanian crew.

sources.title: CNN transcript: kidnapped journalist Phil Sands recounts ordeal
sources.notes: Phil Sands describes the Baghdad kidnapping in first-person terms after his release, confirming a street ambush and hidden custody.

sources.title: Abducted British journalist freed in Iraq
sources.notes: The Irish Times reports that Phil Sands was ambushed in Baghdad on December 26, 2005 and held for five days before release.

sources.title: Indonesians plead for pair’s release
sources.notes: Al Jazeera reports that Meutya Hafid and Budiyanto were pulled from their hired car by armed men near Ramadi while on assignment.

sources.title: Indonesian journalists freed in Iraq
sources.notes: UPI confirms the release of Meutya Hafid and Budiyanto after six days in captivity.

sources.title: Three Romanian journalists abducted in Iraq
sources.notes: Wikinews preserves the public hotel-employee timing report that the kidnapping occurred at approximately 20:30 outside the Flowerland Hotel in Jadriya, while Prima TV lost contact at 19:45.

sources.title: Romanian journalists and translator released
sources.notes: CPJ confirms the release of the Romanian journalists and their translator after nearly two months in captivity.

sources.title: Richard Butler: A Hostage’s Story
sources.notes: Butler recounts being awakened in his Basra hotel room by armed men dressed as police and taken into custody.

sources.title: British journalist freed after Iraqi army raid
sources.notes: ABC confirms that Butler and his interpreter were seized at gunpoint from their Basra hotel on February 10 and that Butler was released alive in April.

cases.title: Phil Sands abduction
cases.metadata_basis: Same-day reporting plus first-person recollection place the ambush on a bright Baghdad morning on December 26, 2005; the frozen chart uses a mid-morning proxy inside that publicly reported morning window.

hard_outcomes.outcome: released alive after five days in captivity

cases.engine_vs_reality_summary: The live route aligns directionally: abduction fires, violence pressure appears, and the map exposes route/custody roles without drifting into family or accident labels.

tested_anchors.basis: mid-morning proxy inside the publicly reported Baghdad morning ambush window
finding_titles: Life/death overlap points to violence or homicide
Abduction or public-place seizure pattern is active
Moon applying to malefic by hard aspect

map_validation.origin_note: Baghdad city-center proxy is frozen because public reporting identifies the city and seizure type but not the exact block.

cases.title: Meutya Hafid and Budiyanto abduction
cases.metadata_basis: Public reporting places the seizure on the road near Ramadi while the crew was traveling and refueling; the frozen chart uses a late-afternoon route proxy inside that public day window.
cases.engine_vs_reality_summary: The live route aligns on the core pattern: abduction fires cleanly and the map exposes route and hidden-custody roles without the family or disaster spill that would be inconsistent with the public record.

tested_anchors.basis: daytime route proxy inside the publicly reported Ramadi seizure window
finding_titles: Abduction or confrontation-on-the-route pattern is active

map_validation.origin_note: Ramadi city proxy is frozen because the public record describes the route seizure near the city but not a reproducible roadside coordinate.

cases.title: Romanian journalists Jadriya abduction
cases.metadata_basis: A public hotel-employee account places the seizure at approximately 20:30 outside the Flowerland Hotel in Jadriya, while the newsroom lost contact at 19:45.

hard_outcomes.location: Jadriya / Flowerland Hotel area, Baghdad, Iraq
hard_outcomes.outcome: released alive on 2005-05-22 after 55 days in captivity
known_scene_markers: later evidence of coordinated deception by insiders

cases.engine_vs_reality_summary: After the generalization audit, the social-setting indicator remains visible but is context-only because the chart lacks a distinct coercion/custody classifier. The known abduction is therefore retained as a directional miss.

tested_anchors.basis: hotel-employee report of an approximately 20:30 seizure outside the Flowerland Hotel
finding_titles: Abduction or social-gathering seizure pattern is active

map_validation.origin_note: Jadriya district proxy is frozen because the public record identifies the hotel area but not a reliable present-day geocoder result for the original hotel frontage.

cases.title: Richard Butler Basra hotel abduction
cases.metadata_basis: Butler's own account confirms a middle-of-the-night hotel-room seizure by men dressed as police; the frozen chart uses a 02:30 proxy on the public hotel point.

hard_outcomes.outcome: released alive on 2008-04-14 after roughly two months in captivity

cases.engine_vs_reality_summary: The live route now aligns directionally. It no longer leaks into disaster language and instead surfaces a deceptive public-assignment seizure pattern that matches the fake-police hotel-room kidnapping and concealed captivity described in the public record.

tested_anchors.basis: middle-of-the-night hotel seizure reconstructed from Butler's own account
finding_titles: Abduction or deceptive public-assignment seizure pattern is active

map_validation.origin_note: A stable public hotel point is frozen for the Sultan Palace Hotel because the event is venue-specific and map testing should not depend on live geocoder drift.
